clock_meridiem_night: "gecə" (night) scopes the clock to the NIGHT band, which crosses midnight --
it is NOT a uniform +12 PM shift.  "gecə saat üçdə" is three at night 03:00
(small hours, AM), while "gecə saat doqquz" is nine at night 21:00 (late
evening, PM); "gecə saat on iki" is midnight 00:00.  The resolver applies the
midnight-crossing band-split (small hours 1..5 -> AM, evening 6..11 -> PM,
twelve -> midnight).  (Azərbaycan dilinin izahlı lüğəti, s.v. "gecə".)
clock_meridiem_pm: Azerbaijani leads with the daypart adverbial exactly as Turkish does:
"axşam saat səkkizdə" is the ordinary way to say eight in the evening. The
explanatory dictionary glosses "saat" as vaxt, çağ, an, zaman and
illustrates it with "axşam saatlarında" -- the daypart word standing before
the hour noun (Azərbaycan dilinin izahlı lüğəti, s.v. "saat").

named_day_2: az.wiktionary, entry "gün": "Biri gün (o birisi gün) -- sabahdan sonrakı
gün" (the day after tomorrow).  The fused spelling is the one that runs in
literary prose: az.wikisource has "sabah-birigün ərə gedərsən" (Şamdan bəy)
and "sabah yox, birigün züvvarlar çıxırlar" (Danabaş kəndinin əhvalatları).
The bare spaced "biri gün" is deliberately NOT listed -- it collides with
the ordinary "biri" + a gün- word ("başçılardan biri günah işlədərək",
"heç biri günümüzə"), which the fused and the "o ..." forms cannot.
